These has been considered for designing the overall plant. 9.0 Cost Result Report Techno-economic analysis for the project has been done considering the stand-alone operation of the carbon capture project. All the transfer of gases from the project to existing operations or vice-versa have been considered at opportunity cost. Additionally, the project is very different than the reference document of TEA of the electricity generation unit i.e., “Cost and Performance Baseline for Fossil Energy Plants Volume 1: Bituminous Coal and Natural Gas to Electricity”. BF gas is generated from a blast furnace while producing hot metal. This is one of the significant sources of CO , contributing over 60% of total 2 CO emissions. BF gas is lean in energy content compared to natural gas and coal. So, techno-economic 2 parameter comparison with respect to electricity production will not justify the project. However, the project will significantly impact the decarbonization of integrated steel plant operations using the BF- BOF route. So, the life cycle analysis of the project is estimated based on annual CO capture capacity 2 only. 9.1 Methodology and Approach The cost estimation for this project has been done according to NETL (National Energy Technology Laboratory)
